subject: Categorical IV, Continuous Mediators, and Binary DV

messages.author: 0cd2f4cc2800c18b
messages.subject: Categorical IV, Continuous Mediators, and Binary DV
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am doing moderated mediation analysis and unfortunately I am struggling with small problems:

About the model:
I have one categorical IV: reit, repl, control
Two parallel mediators: Med_Emo, Med_Amb,
One serial mediator, which is influenced by Med_Emo and Med_Amb: AV_Per
One binary DV: Choice

med.txt <- '
Med_Emo ~ a1*reit + a2*repl
Med_Amb ~ a3*reit + a4*repl
AV_Pers ~ b1*Med_Emo + b2*Med_Amb + c1*reit + c2*repl
Choice ~ d1*AV_Pers + e1*Med_Emo + e2*Med_Amb + f1*reit + f2*repl

ind1:= a1*b1
ind2:= a2*b1
ind3:= a3*b2
ind4:= a4*b2
ind5:= a1*b1*d1
ind6:= a2*b1*d1
ind7:= a3*b2*d1
ind8:= a4*b2*d1

Modmed1:= ind6 - ind5
Modmed2:= ind8 - ind7
'

med.fit <- sem(med.txt, data = S1, ordered = c("Choice"), estimator = "WLS", se = "bootstrap", bootstrap = 5000)
parameterEstimates(med.fit, ci = TRUE, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple", level = 0.95)



The indirect effects of "(reit,repl,control)" on "choice" are unfortunately very different from the results I get when I do the mediation analysis with SPSS PROCESS .

Can I use Lavaan to run this model or are there any problems which I don't see right now?

I would really appreciate your help. Thank you!!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Categorical IV, Continuous Mediators, and Binary DV
parts: Can I use Lavaan to run this model
are there any problems which I don't see right now?

Don't set estimator = "WLS".  lavaan will automatically set it to DWLS (a specific WLS procedure for categorical data) when you declare any endogenous variables as ordered.  

Not sure results would be comparable to SPSS PROCESS unless you fit the same models.  For example, lavaan fits a (cumulative) probit regression model to (ordered or binary) outcomes, so you would need to use the same in SPSS for results to be comparable.
